findings.failure_path: Git can warn that an untracked directory is unreadable while ls-files returns zero. An unsafe Markdown file inside that directory is then absent from the listing, and the healthy canonical file allows the sweep to pass. The new unreadable-index probe does not exercise this path; the unreadable-directory probe now runs only in fallback mode.
findings.smallest_fix: Treat Git traversal diagnostics indicating an incomplete listing as a named failure, and add an unreadable untracked-directory probe in Git mode.

findings.failure_path: Every rev-parse error is suppressed and interpreted as a plain copy. For example, unreadable Git metadata sends an existing checkout through find, which prunes paths such as .claude even when their Markdown is tracked. This can turn a repository-access failure into a successful, narrower scan.
findings.smallest_fix: Use fallback only when the target genuinely has no Git metadata; otherwise propagate discovery failures through teardown_fail.

findings.failure_path: A top-level offender named '\nunsafe.md' produces an 'offenders\t' line with an empty payload followed by another line. sed extracts only the empty payload, command substitution strips its newline, and teardown_offenders becomes empty. With the canonical file present, the sweep incorrectly passes in either listing mode.
findings.smallest_fix: Determine failure from an explicit offender flag or exit status rather than diagnostic text, escape filenames in diagnostics, and add a leading-newline filename decoy.

findings.failure_path: The new git commit inherits commit.gpgSign and core.hooksPath. On configured developer machines it can prompt, fail, or execute hooks that modify state outside tmp_root before any probe runs. Supplying user.name and user.email does not isolate those behaviors.
findings.smallest_fix: Remove the commit; git add already creates the index needed by ls-files and the unreadable-index probe.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the packet omits the order comparator, mutate/relocate/decoy implementations, and temporary-directory cleanup setup. Consequently, the required section-scoped comparisons, relocation ahead of the section, per-row failure attribution, and cleanup on interrupted permission probes cannot be checked.
findings.smallest_fix: Include those implementation bodies and relevant setup as frozen review context, together with the candidate-bound mutation/control results.

findings.failure_path: The row records that seventeen sabotaged copies each failed for the stated reason, but the supplied sabotage evidence says the run was in progress at packet time. The referenced validation record is absent, so the completed-success assertion exceeds the available evidence.
findings.smallest_fix: Mark the seventeen-case run pending until completed results are available, or attach the completed results bound to this candidate before retaining the assertion.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: root AGENTS.md requires make test for script/reference changes and explicitly says check-ccl-skills.sh is only preliminary screening. The packet supplies focused-walk and validator claims, but no full-lane results or declared deviation. Regressions in other consumers of this shared fixture therefore remain unverified.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply current-candidate results for make test and applicable additional contract checks, including failures or skips and their disposition.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The ordinary content predicates match acceptance, but Git enumeration and report parsing can miss offenders.
The new scratch commit can execute inherited hooks outside the temporary directory. Cleanup and interruption handling are omitted from the packet.
Nonzero listing and classification results are handled, but Git discovery errors and successful commands with traversal warnings can fail open.
The added decoys cover several predicates, but omitted ordering and mutation helpers prevent verification of scoped ordering and right-reason attribution.
The changes address the existing guard; the scratch commit introduces unnecessary signing and hook dependencies.
No product-state migration is introduced. Reverting restores the previous tests, but cannot reverse arbitrary inherited-hook side effects.
Explicit failures have named messages, but incomplete Git traversal can still report success, and raw filenames can corrupt report framing.
The register asserts seventeen completed sabotage successes while the profile describes that run as still in progress.
The shared safety guard remains bypassable through incomplete enumeration and newline-containing filenames.
Required full-lane validation is not evidenced. The scratch commit also conflicts with the local deterministic-validator requirement.
